quarterly_data.quarter: Tazmo results briefing Q&A: Q2 FY2026 Financial Results Briefing (08-19-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Orders and Taiwan OSAT demand, management (results briefing Q&A): in semiconductor equipment, coater/developers and debond cleaners (debonding and cleaning equipment) drove orders; Q1 and Q2 orders rose sharply, but management does not expect the same level to continue in Q3 and Q4 - it has heard that Taiwan foundry and OSAT capex will continue, so orders should continue to some extent though below the first-half level. With advanced packaging work flowing to Taiwan OSATs, which are accelerating capex, Tazmo is receiving inquiries and orders from Taiwan OSATs for debond cleaners and coater/developers. The large Q2 coater/developer order came from a limited number of Taiwan OSATs, building on Tazmo's continued deliveries to them; management infers two drivers: rising conventional wafer-level packaging demand (PCs, tablets) and part of the advanced-packaging process moving from a Taiwan foundry to OSATs, in steps that appear to use Tazmo's coater/developers. Coater/developer margins are not expected to differ much from debond cleaners, with clear volume benefits. For 2027, current orders deliver and are booked as sales next year, so order intake is expected to settle somewhat; management does not currently expect the current high order value to continue as is.

quarterly_data.quarter: Tazmo results briefing Q&A: Q2 FY2026 Financial Results Briefing (08-19-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Surface Treatment Equipment, management (results briefing Q&A): few makers can build plating equipment and supply is said to be short of demand; Tazmo may win further orders but sees no specific projects or amounts yet and will take projects within current production capacity. Substrate-transfer capacity is rising through the expansion of and investment in the Vietnam plant. This segment's substrate transfer carries printed circuit boards and multilayer / build-up boards, not silicon wafers (Tazmo's own Transfer Equipment handles glass substrates, silicon wafers and masks). Compared with the large orders of a few years ago, equipment size is similar, but this time Tazmo won a sizeable batch of wet-process plating equipment. Management expects surface-treatment orders to continue: advanced packages, including AI, always need printed circuit boards, edge AI and physical AI raise the importance of substrates for high-end processors and packages, and EV / vehicle electrification looks to be pausing near term but should grow long term.

quarterly_data.quarter: Tazmo results briefing Q&A: Q2 FY2026 Financial Results Briefing (08-19-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Capacity roadmap, management (results briefing Q&A): units, modules and parts machining are being expanded through the TAZMO VIETNAM plant expansion and added staff, with the Vietnam site playing a major role in raising capacity for surface-treatment substrate transfer and Tazmo's own transfer equipment; semiconductor manufacturing equipment is running at full in-house utilisation, so collaboration with partner companies is most important, and more partners have been added from last year into this year; wet surface-treatment equipment capacity will come from the main production plant in Dongguan, China, and outsourcing. Fixed-asset investment includes a plan, in progress, to set up facilities in Taiwan housing demo equipment for customer evaluation and service and support; R&D spending is up sharply from last year as experimental and demo machines are built on element development that is largely finished, with no major change to the R&D plan.

quarterly_data.quarter: Tazmo results briefing Q&A: Q2 FY2026 Financial Results Briefing (08-19-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Full-year plan, management (results briefing Q&A): the full-year plan does not assume continued acceptance delays - the first-half delay arose in a few specific, highly developmental tools; transfer-equipment orders have grown strongly and, with short lead times, more projects ordered this year may be booked as sales this year than planned, so the full year is expected to proceed broadly in line with plan.

quarterly_data.quarter: Tazmo results briefing Q&A: Q2 FY2026 Financial Results Briefing (08-19-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: New bonders, management (results briefing Q&A): DTB (Direct Transfer Bonding) is a bonder for chip-on-wafer; Tazmo showed it in a panel display at ECTC in the US in May 2026 and is steadily proposing the new technology. LAB (Laser Assist Bonder), also for MEMS, has progressed from an experimental machine to an alpha machine and is moving toward concrete sales; one unit was ordered in Q2 - a very small share of total orders - and sales are expected to widen gradually.
